chunks: There is no one among the believers whose death is more beloved to Iblis than the death of a jurist (faqih).

key_terms.إِبْلِيسَ: Iblis — the personal name of Satan; the one who refused to prostrate before Adam and became the arch-enemy of humanity
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The believers; those who have true faith (iman)
key_terms.فَقِيهٍ: A scholar deeply versed in Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh); one with deep understanding of religious law and its sources

ai.seo_question: Why is the death of a Muslim scholar (faqih) more beloved to Satan than any other believer's death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that among all the deaths of believers, none brings greater joy to Iblis (Satan) than the death of a religious scholar (faqih). This hadith underscores the vital role that knowledgeable scholars play in guiding and protecting the Muslim community from misguidance. The loss of a faqih leaves the community vulnerable to Iblis's deceptions, which is why their passing is celebrated by the enemy of humanity.
